title: DEVOPS role and the runtime lane: one agent on the running deployment
requestedSolution: Owner, 2026-11-27: add a devops preset/role the orchestrator can use. Runtime deployment, switching the dev/prod version and cleanups were being delegated as several tasks to several agents, and those agents interrupted each other; the orchestrator must be more careful about parallelism that is not interruptive to actively running agents.

businessOutcome.problem: The running deployment has no owner role. A restart, a version switch or a cleanup is handed to whichever role looks idle, and two such tasks can run at once: the second restart ends the children of the first task, and a version switch changes the runtime the first task is still measuring. The delegation rules name a shared file, a shared contract and a shared seat as the things that serialise work, but not the shared runtime, and no gate refuses a second live deployment task.
businessOutcome.outcome: A devops preset (role DEVOPS) owns the runtime lane: it is the one role delegated to change the running deployment, it takes a version snapshot, makes one change, proves it from outside the process and leaves the environment clean. The orchestrator policy names the shared runtime as a serialising resource, requires reading running children before ordering a restart, and tells the root to send runtime work to DEVOPS. delegate_task refuses a second live DEVOPS task in the same chat and names the open one, so a deployment is measured and accepted before the next one starts.

make verify and make test are green on the final tree, including the tool-families budget for devops

current.name: Runtime work goes to whatever role is idle
steps: The owner asks for a deploy, a dev/prod version switch or a cleanup
The orchestrator opens one or more tasks and delegates them to roles whose tools fit the commands
Two agents touch the same deployment: one restarts or rebuilds while the other is still proving the previous state
The restart ends the other task's child, the version under measurement changes under it, or two processes fight over the port and the state directory
The board reports blocked tasks and the human restarts the work

target.name: DEVOPS owns the runtime lane, one live task at a time
steps: The owner asks for a runtime change; the orchestrator opens it as a task whose acceptance is the change measured from outside the deployment
The orchestrator delegates it to DEVOPS, and checks the board for tasks with running children, naming the ones a restart would end
The devops child reads the board, records the version it replaces, changes one thing, verifies the live deployment, and cleans up what it created
The orchestrator accepts the result and closes the task; only then may the next deployment task start
Unrelated work keeps running in parallel, because it touches no file, contract, seat or runtime that the deployment touches

invariants.text: A role label keeps one preset; existing labels and presets are not re-composed.
Every refusal in delegate_task happens before a task row exists and before a child starts.
One live devops task per chat; a task is live while it is open, active, blocked or paused.
Other roles keep their current surfaces and may still batch several rows into one seat.

decisions.decision: Add a preset instead of extending BACKEND
decisions.rationale: SEGMENTATION and CONCURRENCY already share backend's tools and differ only in persona; the runtime lane needs its own tool set (long background jobs, jobs, web for releases) and its own seat, so a name would have been a persona without a boundary.

decisions.decision: Enforce one live devops task; leave other roles' batch attach alone
decisions.rationale: A batch of rows into one seat is the intended cheap pattern for implementation and review, but a deployment has to be measured and accepted before the next one replaces the runtime it measured.

decisions.decision: Refuse by task state, not by keywords in the brief
decisions.rationale: A word list cannot tell 'restart the stand' from 'read the restart section of the docs', so the gate keys on the ledger's own status of a task whose role resolves to devops.

decisions.decision: Do not restart the live :3080 deployment from this session
decisions.rationale: A restart ends this session mid-turn; composition is proven on a second server and the live server converges on its next ./start.sh.

decisions.decision: Pin High per working preset instead of relying on the machine default
decisions.rationale: kit-update keeps the installed agent-default-model row verbatim (this machine carries sol at xhigh), so the deployment default alone would never reach a working role; a role-model rule is the seam kit-update does update.

decisions.decision: Put the development rules in ROOT_POLICY, keep the skill as the long form
decisions.rationale: A rule that must bind every step cannot depend on someone loading a skill; the owner's ten-defect observation showed the class is found by running, so the short rules (one owner per rule, tool is not behaviour, prove by running, smallest change, name what was skipped) belong in the prompt, with the full skill for the rare deep pass.

decisions.decision: Make the scope a path claim keyed on active tasks, not a lock file or a write-time check
decisions.rationale: The claim has to exist at delegation time, before two children start: the taskboard's active status is the one durable fact about work in flight, and the scope list is already in every brief. A keyword or directory-only rule would either block disjoint files in one directory or miss the file case; a write-time check would report the collision after both children had edited it.

reasons: A new preset inside the existing profile plus a refusal in delegate_task

The live server is not restarted; composition is proven on a second server
